transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been making mistakes at work that I really know better than to make. I’m a camera operator and editor, and lately I’ll do things like label camera cards wrong, miss a timecode note, or export a client cut with the wrong lower-third, even after I thought I checked it. It’s happened enough that it kind of scared me.
Have you noticed any other changes in your thinking, memory, or concentration besides the mistakes at work?

Yeah, I’ve noticed it when people are talking to me too. Like on set, a producer will give me a note directly, and I’m looking right at them, but my mind has already jumped ahead to the lens change or the next shot. Then I realize I didn’t actually take in what they said, and I have to ask them to repeat it. It’s embarrassing because I was standing right there.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy? Or have you been feeling unusually anxious lately?

I don’t think so, not in a major way. I mean, I get frustrated and stressed when I mess something up, but I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless or that I’ve stopped enjoying things. And I’m not walking around feeling anxious all the time.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

No, I don’t think so. I have days where I feel wound up or busy, but not like unusually energized in that way, and I don’t really go without sleep and feel fine. I wouldn’t say my thoughts are racing like that.
Have you had trouble with focusing or staying on task in other areas of your life, like at home or in conversations, not just at work?

Yeah, it happens in conversations too. Like if a producer gives me a direct note on set, I’ll be looking right at them, but my brain has already moved on to the lens change or the next shot. Then I realize I didn’t actually hear the note, and I have to ask them to say it again, which feels pretty embarrassing.
Have you noticed any difficulty with memory, such as forgetting things you were just told, or trouble keeping track of everyday tasks like paying bills or remembering appointments?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think I’m forgetting appointments or bills in a big way. Sometimes I need someone to repeat something, like I said, but for everyday memory stuff… I haven’t noticed a clear pattern.
Have you ever had trouble sitting still, felt restless, or acted on impulse without thinking, like interrupting others or making quick decisions without considering the consequences?

Yeah, sitting still can be hard. Like during a client screening, when I know I’m supposed to just sit there and watch quietly, it feels like pressure is building under my skin. I get this strong need to get up or do something with my body, even if I know I shouldn’t.
Have you had any medical conditions or neurological issues that might affect your brain function, such as seizures, head injuries, strokes, or any chronic illnesses like diabetes or hypertension?
Not that I know of. I don’t have anything like that that I’m aware of. I mean, no major medical or neurological issue comes to mind.
Have you noticed any decline in your thinking or memory compared to how you functioned in the past, even a few months or a year ago?
No, I haven’t really noticed a decline like that. I feel like I’m functioning about the same as I was a few months or a year ago. Nothing stands out to me as getting worse with my thinking or memory.

Do you find yourself getting distracted easily or having trouble staying focused on tasks or activities in other parts of your life, like reading, watching a movie, or even just having a conversation at home?

Yeah, that happens. Like on set, a producer can be giving me a direct note and I’m looking right at them, but my mind has already jumped to the lens change or the next shot. Then I realize I didn’t actually take in what they said, and I have to ask them to repeat it.
When did you first notice these issues with distraction and not being able to stay focused?

Honestly, I think it goes way back. Even in elementary school, I remember teachers moving my desk because I was always getting out of my seat, blurting out answers, or distracting other kids before I even realized I was doing it.
Do you find it hard to organize tasks, manage your time, or follow through on responsibilities, even when you understand what needs to be done?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I understand what needs to be done most of the time, but I’d have to think more about whether organizing or time management is a big issue for me. Nothing specific is coming to mind right now.
As a child, did you have difficulty staying seated, waiting your turn, or often feel restless?

Yes, definitely. In elementary school I was always getting out of my seat, or blurting out answers before it was my turn. Teachers would move my desk because I’d be bothering classmates, and honestly I don’t think I even realized I was doing it at the time.
Do you find these issues with focus and restlessness happen in other areas of your life outside of work, such as at home, in personal relationships, or during leisure activities?

I’m not totally sure how much it shows up outside of work. I mean, I can feel restless in general sometimes, but I’d have to think about whether it really affects home or relationships in a clear way. Nothing specific is coming to mind right now.
